native_mechanisms: A stone on a corner: a vertex's distance becomes final once settled and is never reconsidered.
A duck carries a spooled thread: each frontier vertex holds a tentative label equal to the running sum of edge lengths along the path that reached it.
Each round, the leader duck is found — the shortest carried thread among the unstoned — and settled before any other duck moves.
(prose only) Roads toward houses with no far side are thrown away unspooled — dead-end vertices are never queued.
(prose only) Trace every shot back to its landing before trusting the leader — stale/superseded entries are rejected.
core_technique: Dijkstra's algorithm over a CSR adjacency, with a compact unordered array of active tentative labels scanned by an AVX2 argmin for extract-min plus O(1) positional decrease-key, falling back to a lazy-deletion 4-ary binary heap once the frontier exceeds a computed threshold; sink vertices are pruned from the frontier.
